articles.title: ‘Embarrassing,’ ‘Hard Watch’ — CFB Fans Clown Kentucky Fan for Weak Heckling of Alabama QB Keelon Russell and Co.
articles.summary: Kentucky coach Will Stein spent the week begging Wildcats fans to make Kroger Field miserable for Alabama. One fan apparently took the assignment seriously,...
articles.body:
Kentucky coach Will Stein spent the week begging Wildcats fans to make Kroger Field miserable for Alabama. One fan apparently took the assignment seriously, even if the execution drew considerably more laughter than intimidation.

A video shared by AL.com's Alabama account showed a Kentucky fan heckling Keelon Russell and other Crimson Tide players from close range before Saturday's SEC matchup.

Instead of praising the trash talk, viewers mostly roasted the heckler, with reactions ranging from "Embarrassing" to describing the clip as a "Hard Watch."

CFB Fans Roast Kentucky Heckler Before Alabama Game

One fan did not bother with a long review, writing, "Embarrassing."

Another user focused on the age gap between the heckler and Alabama's young quarterback, writing, "That freshman who should be 'partying' is half that guys age and more successful than he'll ever be 😭😭."

PREDICT THE CFB SEASON: PFN's Free CFB Playoff Predictor

A third fan was left wondering whether Kentucky had anything sharper available, writing, "That's the best they have?"

The mockery kept coming. Another user wrote, "Really got him with that one!! Possibly the worst trash talk I've ever heard."

One more fan offered a simple piece of advice: "if u gone heckle atleast be funny."

The reaction was especially amusing given Stein's own buildup to the game. Earlier in the week, Kentucky's first-year coach encouraged fans to create an uncomfortable environment for Alabama, calling on the crowd to be as loud as possible and even urging supporters to "scream obscenities."

If the goal was to get under Alabama's skin, social media seemed unconvinced this particular attempt qualified.

Keelon Russell Faces First SEC Road Test

The timing made Russell a natural target. Saturday marked his first road start and first SEC start since winning Alabama's quarterback job in August.

Russell opened his starting career by helping No. 12 Alabama beat East Carolina 48-10 in Week 1. He entered Saturday ranked No. 41 in PFN's current QB Impact rankings, with the former five-star prospect still early in his development as Kalen DeBoer's full-time starter.

Kentucky entered the matchup seeking its first victory over Alabama since 1997. The Wildcats had lost eight straight meetings since that upset, giving a packed Kroger Field plenty of reason to make Russell's afternoon uncomfortable.

At the latest live check, Kentucky led Alabama 14-13 with two minutes remaining in the second quarter, and Russell had completed 8 of 10 passes for 123 yards with 1 interception.

That interception came on Alabama's opening drive and was returned for a Kentucky touchdown, giving the home crowd exactly the sort of early jolt Stein had requested.

The Wildcats were doing a much better job making Russell uncomfortable on the field than the viral heckler managed from the stands.

For the fan in the video, the internet's review was considerably harsher than anything he managed to deliver to Alabama.

articles.title: Mike Vrabel doubles down on preseason decision, despite backlash
articles.summary: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel has no regrets about resting the starters during the preseason.
articles.body:
New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel doesn't have any regrets about his decision to rest the starters during the three-game preseason slate.

However, it was clear that the team showed rust in Wednesday's 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks , particularly on the offensive side of the ball. Vrabel opted to use the preseason to focus on the roster depth and preserve the health of the starters.

That's a decision that he continued to defend after the disappointing loss in the season opener.

"Playing the backups for the Eagles or the Colts for eight plays, I don't think was going to prepare us for what we saw last night," Vrabel told media members. "I thought we handled the environment; I thought we did. I know the execution wasn't good enough, but the line of scrimmage, penalties, the operation, those things gave us a chance. Some other things didn't give us a chance."

Patriots quarterback Drake Maye threw three interceptions, and the team lost star wide receiver A.J. Brown to a high ankle sprain, which will keep him sidelined for at least the next four games.

The team is hopeful that the worst is behind them with the Pittsburgh Steelers next on the schedule. They'll be back at home at Gillette Stadium before back-to-back games on the road at Jacksonville and Buffalo.

It's only one week, and there's already a sense of urgency for the Patriots.

Follow Patriots Wire on Twitter and Facebook .

articles.title: Is help coming for the Cubs bullpen at a critical time?
articles.summary: With about two weeks left in the regular season, the Cubs have an uncomfortable problem. Their offense is the best in baseball. By a lot. Their defense is th...
articles.body:
With about two weeks left in the regular season, the Cubs have an uncomfortable problem. Their offense is the best in baseball. By a lot. Their defense is the best in baseball. By even more. But their pitching, specifically the bullpen, is a glaring Achilles' Heel .

According to Fangraphs' wins above replacement, the Cubs ' arms are last in baseball. There are a lot of variables to measuring a pitching staff, but even an attentive observer doesn't need the metrics to know the Cubs pitching is a problem.

Specifically, the Cubs' bullpen. They upgraded the rotation at the trade deadline, bringing in Kevin Gausman and Clay Holmes . And although the results on that front have been a bit mixed, there's still little question that the bullpen isn't one built for a postseason series. At times lately it's been unclear whether they're good enough to help keep the Cubs in one of the wild card spots.

The good news is that some help is here, and more could be coming.

Before Saturday's 4-3 win over the Pirates, Edward Cabrera was activated from the injured list, swapping places with Trent Thornton , who manager Craig Counsell said is having left ankle issues. Enthusiasm over Cabrera's return might be tempered, given his 5.68 ERA and multiple trips to the IL this season, but with the raw potential of his stuff, Cabrera could end up being a crucial piece in a Cubs' playoff bullpen.

In fact, Counsell likened his potential to Dodgers pitcher Roki Sasaki 's move from the rotation to the bullpen during their postseason run in 2025.

"That could happen, that's an example," he said. "That's a roadmap to how this can be really successful. Was that the best result? That was probably a pretty darn good result, but I think that's what you keep yourself open to.

"We don't know that we're going to get there, but it's a good blueprint that you can hope to repeat."

Counsell said the idea resonated with Cabrera when he spoke to him about pitching out of the bullpen. Cabrera has little professional experience in that role, but for his part, Cabrera is at least saying the right things.

"When he talked to me, that was the example that was given to me, and I'm going to go out there and give it my best," Cabrera said through team interpreter Fredy Quevedo, Jr.

Even if he is lights out coming from the 'pen, Cabrera alone isn't going to right the ship. The Cubs need other guys to get going, too. Daniel Palencia , for example, returned from the injured list a few weeks ago, but is not pitching at all like the guy who closed out the World Baseball Classic back in March.

On that front, Counsell said he thinks the best way to get Palencia back on track is to keep giving him innings. As illustrated by CHGO's Brendan Miller , there has been a significant decrease in movement on Palencia's pitches, which is making them much more hittable. Triple-digit speed alone isn't enough to get guys out anymore.

"Whether is the delivery on a fastball, the execution of a slider that makes a hitter swing and miss, [a game] is where the best feedback is going to come, and the feedback that is going to build your confidence," Counsell said.

There's also the tantalizing story of Justin Steele's imminent return . He's been pitching well in his rehab outings with the Triple-A Iowa Cubs, and Counsell said Steele will throw a bullpen session in front of the Chicago pitching coaches at Wrigley on Sunday before returning to Iowa to make at least one more rehab appearance.

From there, it's possible Steele is rejoining the big league ballclub for the first time since April 2025 as early as the Cubs' series in Cincinnati . But even if that does happen, it's unlikely that Steele is doing much more than picking up a few mid-leverage innings in the last eight or nine games of the season. He might not even be a guy who makes a postseason roster.

Which brings us back to Cabrera, and to some extent, Palencia too. The Cubs' pitching woes won't be solved by one guy, but either — or, a fanbase can dream, both — pitching to the potential that they have will go a long way toward stabilizing a bullpen that's been more than a bit wobbly.

Cabrera didn't appear in Saturday's game, but the relievers Counsell used held the Pirates' lead to one run so that a pair of timely pinch-hit walks by Matt Shaw and Seiya Suzuki in the 8th inning could put the Cubs ahead.

Jacob Webb picked up starter Clay Holmes in the sixth inning and then pitched a scoreless seventh before Ryan Rolison pitched the eighth and the first two outs of the ninth inning. Ryan Zeferjahn struck out Bryan Reynolds looking to end the game.

All three of these are pitchers who have struggled recently, most notably Webb. He had a rough road trip through Seattle and Arizona in late August, and he gave up late leads twice against the Brewers this month. Webb has also had long stretches of being untouchable for the Cubs, but this late in the season, and especially against Milwaukee , his struggles have been costly.

But coming into a high-leverage spot in Saturday's win over Pittsburgh , Webb delivered. With the Cubs trailing by a run and the bases loaded, Webb got Oneil Cruz to ground out to second. He pitched around a leadoff walk to deliver a scoreless seventh.

Those are the kinds of outings that help a reliever flush the tough ones, and for Webb, he doesn't like too much time to dwell on the hard days.

"I almost want to go back out there as quick as possible," he said. "I don't want to sit on it. I want to get back out there and work on my stuff or just have a better outing in general."

The Cubs aren't going to fix all that ails them in the next two weeks, but there is precedent for teams who hit well and play great defense but pitch poorly still being able to succeed in the playoffs. There are a number of Yankees teams of the 1920s and 30s who won that way, as did Cincinnati of Big Red Machine fame in the 1970s.

But more than just hoping they can outfield and outslug everyone, the Cubs might have to course correct, even if slightly, but taking an uncomfortable problem and leaning into unfamiliar roles.

"When you get to this time of year, we have to accept some discomfort because we have to do what's best for the team," Counsell said.

articles.title: Vincent Kompany riffs on how to deal with Bayern Munich’s Sacha Boey
articles.summary: Kompany explains Boey’s situation at FC Bayern.
articles.body:
Despite Bayern Munich having made it clear that Sacha Boey was not in Vincent Kompany's plans for this season, the defender was unable to find a destination away from the German Rekordmeister during the summer transfer window. There was interest from Turkey and even Fulham at one point towards the end of the transfer window, but nothing wound up materializing for the Frenchmen, and he's now been forced to make do at Bayern despite being well out of favor and a surplus to requirements.

What's equally as frustrating for Boey is that both Bryan Zaragoza and João Palhinha wound up finding clubs as the other two players that Bayern made clear they would be trying to sell during the summer window. Nonetheless, Boey has at least remained increasingly professional in what's a bit of a tricky situation for the player, which the club does greatly appreciate. The plan is to reassess options in the winter transfer window to see if they can find a solution that's bet for all parties.

Ahead of Bayern's Bundesliga clash against SV Elversberg, Kompany spoke about Boey's situation and said that is always best for the club to be 100% honest and transparent with its players. "What I've seen in the past two-and-a-half years of working with Max Eberl and Christoph Freund is that the club is clear and straightforward, also in its dealings with the players. It's not always pleasant for the player, but you also gain a lot of respect from the players when you speak to them clearly and honestly. Now the transfer window is closed, and Sacha is part of our team and has our support. My role now is that he performs," he explained (via @iMiaSanMia ).

While rotations will be made by Kompany as Bayern pushes across three fronts and injuries will naturally occur over the course of the season, the Belgian can't even guarantee Boey any time with the depth Bayern has in defense. Even Kompany knows that so many different things could wind up happening between now and the start of the January transfer window. "The reality is that we have Josip Stanišić and Konrad Laimer in the position, and the competition is already fierce. So you need patience and hard work. But anything can happen in football if you have the right attitude. We're simply treating him with respect. He's training very well at the moment, and everything else will fall into place," Kompany stressed.

articles.title: Beau Brungard accounts for 8 TDs as Youngstown State cruises past Duquesne 70-13
articles.summary: Beau Brungard accounted for eight touchdowns — seven coming in the first half — and Youngstown State cruised past Duquesne 70-13 on Saturday.  Brungard set a...
articles.body:
YOUNGSTOWN, Ohio (AP) — Beau Brungard accounted for eight touchdowns — seven coming in the first half — and Youngstown State cruised past Duquesne 70-13 on Saturday.

Brungard set a single-game school record with his sixth touchdown pass. Backup Malachi Lewis added 117 yards passing and a score to set another school record for total touchdown passes in a game.

Brungard finished 20 of 23 for 290 yards passing and six touchdowns for Youngstown State (2-1), which is ranked No. 10 in the Stats Perform poll. Brungard led the team with 14 carries for 111 yards and two scores — for his 12th career game with 100-plus passing and rushing yards.

Brungard was 16 of 19 for 256 yards and six touchdowns in the first half. He also rushed 12 times for 101 yards and another score. Brungard capped a 75-yard drive in the third quarter with a short touchdown run to make it 56-10.

Lynn Wyche-El had four catches for 73 yards and two touchdowns in the first half. Bryan Hunt, Dorian Williams , Jeremiah Sanders and Jaden Gilbert also had a touchdown grab by halftime.

Duquesne (0-2) was held to 13 first downs and 244 total yards.

Duquesne: At Washington State next Saturday.

Youngstown State: At South Dakota State next Saturday.

articles.title: NFL picks: Experts all pick Chargers over Cardinals in Week 1
articles.summary: Nobody is picking the Cardinals to upset the Chargers in Week 1.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals will face the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday in Week 1. The Cardinals are big underdogs, coming off a 3-14 season. The Chargers had a top-10 defense in 2025 and made the playofs for the second straight season and third time in four years.

As such, the Cardinals are not a popular pick to win this week.

What do experts say? Here are some picks and predictions from NFL experts.

Jess Root, Cards Wire: Chargers 31, Cardinals 17

While the Cardinals' offense is promising, this is an awful matchup for them. The Chargers were a top-10 defense in points, yards, first downs, pass defense and run defense. They have great edge players in Khalil Mack and Tuli Tuipulotu , so the Cardinals will not be able to thrive against that defense.

And the Chargers' offensive problems in 2025 should be in the past with new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. Arizona's defense will struggle, and the offense won't be able to keep up.

Seth Cox, SB Nation and Rise Up, See Red Podcast: Chargers 27, Cardinals 20

The 10 experts pick the Chargers unanimously. Eight believe the Chargers will have a double-digit win.

We will see what happens on Sunday. The game kicks off at 4:25 p.m. ET (1:25 p.m. Arizona time) Sunday afternoon at SoFi Stadium.

Get more Cardinals and NFL coverage from Cards Wire's Jess Root and others by listening to the latest on the Rise Up, See Red podcast. Subscribe on Spotify , YouTube or Apple Podcasts .

articles.title: Alaska sports notebook: UAA volleyball dominates in first GNAC win, Dimond volleyball continues to roll
articles.summary: Sep. 12—After having its multi-match winning streak snapped on the road last week, the University of Alaska Anchorage volleyball team bounced back with a ven...
articles.body:
Sep. 12—After having its multi-match winning streak snapped on the road last week, the University of Alaska Anchorage volleyball team bounced back with a vengeance on Thursday night at the Alaska Airlines Center.

The Seawolves swept Seattle Pacific in three straight sets to pick up their first Great Northwest Athletic Conference win of the season. They notched a pair of double-doubles as senior outside hitter Lee Ivakina topped the team with 11 kills and 13 digs, while senior setter Hannah Trotter led the team with 27 assists and finished third in digs with 10.

"It was another great team effort tonight, with everyone stepping up to contribute," UAA head coach Morgan Hooe said in a statement. "Hannah did well again at distributing the ball to our attackers, and Patri Ferran (5 kills) had a nice breakout match."

In the Interior, the University of Alaska Fairbanks volleyball team accomplished a similar feat on the same night with a three-set sweep of Montana State Billings at home. The Nanooks were able to do so without a single player reaching double figures in kills. Freshman Cori Leavitt and redshirt sophomore Haylee Lyons tied for the team lead with eight apiece.

On the prep volleyball scene, reigning 4A state champion Dimond cruised to a fifth straight three-set sweep Wednesday night to remain undefeated against in-state competition. The Lynx successfully defended their home court against Bartlett, winning each set by 12 or more points. The Golden Bears were led in kills by senior Ailafo Fautanu with 10, junior libero Evie McKenna led the team with a dozen digs and senior setter Puao Asailevai logged the most assists with 20.

In high school flag football action, perennial contender North Pole increased its winning streak to six in a row with a pair of blowout road victories over Mat-Su Borough School District programs. On Thursday, the Patriots defeated Wasilla 34-13 thanks in large part to three players eclipsing 100 all-purpose yards. Senior running back Jade Skipps led the team with 306 yards she compiled by scoring a trio of touchdowns, including a 77-yard run late in the fourth quarter during which the stadium lights went out as she crossed the 30-yard line.

Second on the team was junior Jordi Darby with 170 all-purpose yards that included a pair of touchdowns and 63 receiving yards, and she also scored on both a two-point and a one-point conversion. Senior Taimane Skipps was a force on both sides of the ball with 128 all-purpose yards, throwing a touchdown, recording two interceptions and leading the team with eight flag pulls.

Anchorage's Brandon Pili helped the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks kick off their title-defending season on a high note Wednesday night in a 13-10 win over the New England Patriots. The former Dimond High standout and fourth-year pro logged nine combined snaps, with six coming on defense and three on special teams.
authors: Josh Reed, Anchorage Daily News, Alaska

articles.title: Clemson Tigers vs. Georgia Southern Eagles: Live Gamethread, Online Streaming, TV Channels
articles.summary: I got nothing here. No hints of optimism, nothing more to say. The only good thing here is that the OL should hopefully figure out how to block something. If...
articles.body:
I got nothing here. No hints of optimism, nothing more to say. The only good thing here is that the OL should hopefully figure out how to block something. If they look like traffic cones again then it is going to be a looooong season.

Normal rules here are no one gets hurt, starters get pulled at halftime, and the backups get plenty of snaps. I'll let y'all bet on how likely that is. Don't be surprised if you see the OL play the entire game regardless of the score. Last week was unacceptable, but this line does not have much experience on the field, only a handful of starts among the 5. This is an opportunity for them to gel.

And if this ends up being like Troy back in 2011? We should all invest heavily in things that make us happy while watching football. Or take up golf or something.

As always, join us in the comments for this one. It can't get any worse, right?

articles.title: Alejandro Kirk hits 2-run homer, Brett Bateman has a solo shot as Blue Jays beat Orioles 7-3
articles.summary: Alejandro Kirk hit a two-run home run, Brett Bateman added a solo shot and the Toronto Blue Jays beat the Baltimore Orioles 7-3 on Saturday afternoon.  Pete...
articles.body:
TORONTO (AP) — Alejandro Kirk hit a two-run home run, Brett Bateman added a solo shot and the Toronto Blue Jays beat the Baltimore Orioles 7-3 on Saturday afternoon.

Pete Alonso hit his 35th home run for Baltimore, a two-run blast off Paul Sewald in the seventh inning, but the Orioles lost for the eighth time in 11 September games.

Kirk had two hits and drove in three as the Blue Jays won for the second time in six games and ensured they would not lose ground in the AL wild card race. Toronto entered two games behind Cleveland for the final playoff spot.

Kirk and Bateman both connected off Orioles right-hander Kyle Bradish (7-14) in the third.

Bateman's first career home run came in the ninth inning of Friday's 7-4 loss . Saturday's was his second.

George Springer singled and Vladimir Guerrero Jr . struck out before Kirk homered to left. Eight of Kirk's 10 homers have come since the All-Star break.

Guerrero scored the first run after an RBI double in the first and came around on Kirk's single.

Spencer Miles opened for Toronto and struck out five in two scoreless innings, allowing one hit and two walks.

Joe Mantiply worked a 1-2-3 third before Spencer Arrighetti (8-9) entered and allowed one unearned run in 2 2/3 innings. Arrighetti walked two and struck out a pair.

Mason Fluharty and Sewald each got two outs, Tyler Rogers worked the eighth and Louis Varland finished for Toronto.

Starting on his 30th birthday, Bradish gave up five runs and eight hits in three innings, his ninth consecutive winless outing. He's 0-5 with a 5.83 ERA since winning at Boston on July 22.

Orioles LHP Trevor Rogers (10-9, 4.15) is scheduled to start for the Orioles on Sunday against RHP Dylan Cease (10-5, 2.40 ERA).

articles.title: Ryan Garcia Vs. Conor Benn Is Over — Here Are The Scorecards And Biggest Highlights
articles.summary: Ryan Garcia battles Conor Benn in one of the most high-profile fights in boxing in 2026. Follow along for the latest updates and results.
articles.body:
The time has come for Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn to put the verbal sparring and angry exchanges aside. The two stars will clash on Saturday night at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas. I'll have live results from the entire card here. Let's talk boxing .

Sean Garcia def. Abraham Morales via Majority Decision (56-56, 58-54, 58-54)

Ryan's younger brother Sean pulls out the victory to open the card. Garcia scored a knockdown with his brother's signature left hook.

Ryan Garcia Vs. Conor Benn Full Card Results

Da'Mazion Vanhouter vs. Raphael Akpejiori

Garcia wins by Majority Decision (56-56, 58-54, 58-54)

The main event has been wrought with trash talk and bad blood, and it is easy to forget this is a title fight. Garcia's WBC welterweight title is on the line. Can Garcia's seemingly superior boxing acumen best Benn's aggression and toughness?

That's the big question and why this is an intriguing fight. The winner of this fight will have a huge fight in front of them, no matter what weight class they go to from here. Benn talked about the weight cut down to welterweight being brutal. And he hinted this would be his final fight at 147 pounds.

If that's the case and he moves up to super welterweight, middleweight or even super middleweight, there will be no shortage of huge fights for him. The opportunities will be even bigger if he beats Garcia.

Welterweight has picked up. Garcia will have major opportunities against the likes of Shakur Stevenson and a rematch with Devin Haney.

In the co-main event, two of the best cruiserweights in the world clash. Jai Opetaia is a pound-for-pound contender who might need to ultimately move up to heavyweight to get a real look on that front. For now, he's got a tough Noel Mikaelian in front of him on one of the biggest boxing cards of 2026.

articles.title: UTSA, Texas State fans battle 100-degree hazardous weather in San Marcos
articles.summary: A sparse crowd was in attendance for the Bobcats' Pac-12 opener.
articles.body:
Last week, fans at Darrel K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium fled into the shade as heat made the Texas vs. Texas State game unbearable to the Austin crowd. Today, the Bobcats returned to San Marcos for their home opener but the heat remained a menace.

Texas State hosted UTSA on Saturday, September 12, as part of the annual I-35 rivalry series. The game also served as the Bobcats' first home game as members of the Pac-12. However the stadium was far from packed as the San Marcos faithful dealt with 100-degree temperatures and hazardous weather conditions, according to the National Weather Service (NWS) .

The X account Bobcat Nation called out the lack of attendance, writing, "Stadium is EMPTY at KickOFF. An Absolute failure by @TXST."

Fans in attendance were quick to reply, writing that many fans were in attendance but hiding from the sun by remaining in the stadium concourse. Others cited college football's lack of understanding Texas weather, saying all September games need to be in the evening to fight the extreme temps.

A stadium shot during the live broadcast put the situation in perspective, showing a large group of fans sitting in the shade while the seats in the sun were almost empty.

San Marcos is expected to see temperature highs of 101 degrees with a heat index as high as 107, according to the NWS. Temperatures could drop as low as 76 degrees this evening with slight chances for showers throughout the night.

images.caption: Ryan Nolan #7 of the Texas State Bobcats celebrates after an interception in the first half against the Texas Longhorns at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium on September 05, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Tim Warner/Getty Images)
